chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

A place would be spread for Abd al-Muttalib in the courtyard of the Ka'bah; it would not be spread for anyone other than him. He had sons who would stand at his head and keep away whoever came near him.

Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came, while he was a small child just beginning to walk, until he sat upon his thighs. One of them moved toward him to remove him from there, so Abd al-Muttalib said to him: 'Leave my son, for the angel has already come to him.'

key_terms.الْمَلَكُ: the angel, indicating divine attendance or protection
key_terms.بِفِنَاءِ الْكَعْبَةِ: in the courtyard of the Ka'bah
key_terms.طِفْلٌ يَدْرِجُ: a small child beginning to walk
key_terms.عَبْدُ الْمُطَّلِبِ: Abd al-Muttalib, the grandfather of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about signs of the Prophet's صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم special status in his childhood?
ai.summary: This narration describes the special stature of Abd al-Muttalib and an early sign of the unique rank of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم during his childhood. It presents Abd al-Muttalib as recognizing divine care surrounding the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, indicating his exceptional status even before his public mission.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Rifa’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> was such that they used to furnish for him<sup>as</sup> in the courtyard of the Kabah. It was not furnished for anyone apart from him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>. And it was so that his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> sons would be standing by his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> head protecting him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> from the ones who approached him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>.

So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> came over, and he<sup>saww</sup> was a child who had begun to walk, until he<sup>saww</sup> came to be upon his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> thigh. So one of them gestured towards him<sup>saww</sup> in order to prevent him<sup>saww</sup> from him<sup>asws</sup>, but Abdul Muttalib<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Leave my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>saww</sup>, for an Angel has come with him<sup>saww</sup>’ (as a servant).
en.sarwar: 26. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Rifa‘Abdallah from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“At a certain place around the Ka‘ba ‘Abd al-Muttalib’s people would spread house furnishings for him only and for no one else. His sons would stand around him for protection.

Once the Messenger of Allah, then a small child who had just began to walk came to ‘Abd al-Muttalib and sat in his lap. One of the people standing as a guard came to remove the child away but ‘Abd al-Muttalib said, “Leave my child alone. The angel has just come to him.”
